newsitem.title: INDIA: Doctors say Mother Teresa stable but test delayed.
newsitem.headline: Doctors say Mother Teresa stable but test delayed.

text.p: Doctors treating Mother Teresa at an Indian heart clinic said on Wednesday her condition was stable but could worsen at any time, forcing them to delay a special X-ray test to see if she needed surgery.
"She is not out of danger now. Things can turn bad at any moment," said Dr Tarun Praharaj, a member of her medical team at the B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre in Calcutta.
"So we are very careful and we will keep her under observation for at least another 24 hours. Then we will decide on angiography," Praharaj told Reuters.
"Mother had some discomfort early this morning," he said. "She was immediately given some medicine and she responded well. She is now stable and sleeping."
Doctors had said earlier that Mother Teresa, 86, might undergo an angiography -- an X-ray of blood vessels to detect arterial blockage -- on Wednesday.
Mother Teresa, known as the "Saint of the Gutters" for her work with the world's poor, was moved on Tuesday from intensive care at the Woodlands Nursing Home to the nearby heart clinic.
Praharaj said on Tuesday night that the Roman Catholic nun's condition was "clinically unstable" and ruled out the test for at least a couple of days.
The 1979 Nobel Peace Prize winner entered the Woodlands Nursing Home early last Friday with an irregular heartbeat.

Fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989, she has twice undergone coronary angiography -- in the United States in 1991 and at the Birla clinic in 1993. Both times she subsequently underwent angioplasty, in which surgeons insert a balloon into an artery, then inflate it to unblock the artery.
Praharaj said the X-ray would show if a third angioplasty was necessary. But he added that Mother Teresa has more separate health problems now, notably a chest infection, than in 1993.

On Tuesday, about 200 people, including nuns from her Missionaries of Charity religious order, watched Mother Teresa, eyes shut and arms folded over her chest, as she was carried from the nursing home on a stretcher.
A doctor, a nurse and four nuns escorted her in the ambulance on the short drive to the heart clinic.
"She has been placed in the critical care unit where all heart-support arrangments are available," clinic administrator A.K. Chatterjee said.
Dr S.K. Sen, the medical director of the Woodlands Nursing Home, said Mother Teresa had ischaemia, or hardening of the arteries. Her heart has failed several times since last Thursday.

She was initially reluctant to undergo any special tests or surgery. But on Tuesday, Sen said she had agreed to undergo angiography, which he described as a very safe procedure involving the injection of dye through a catheter.
The dye shows up on the X-ray, revealing any blockage. Patients are put under general anaesthesia, he said.
Sen said the two doctors who performed angioplasty on Mother Teresa at the Birla centre in 1993 -- Praharaj and Deepak Shetty -- would conduct the angiography.
Dr Patricia Aubanel, who treated her in the United States, had arrived in Calcutta to supervise the procedure, he said.
